Martensite permanent MeshVS volume-topology fixture

Captured from OCCT 8.1.0-dev1, commit 3d097a0328e71b826377d4814ab05ec3c3d23871.
Source: src/Visualization/TKMeshVS/MeshVS/MeshVS_DataSource3D.hxx and .cxx.
Original implementation: Alexander SOLOVYOV, 2005-01-21.
Copyright (c) 2005-2014 OPEN CASCADE SAS.
Upstream license: LGPL 2.1 with OCCT_LGPL_EXCEPTION.txt special exception;
alternative OCCT commercial terms are described in the source notice.

The fixture records actual CreatePrismTopology/CreatePyramidTopology calls,
not a reimplementation of their expected output. Integer rows need no tolerance.
Each of the first 24 rows contains kind, base-point count, null flag, then
(nonnull only) lower/upper face bounds and each face's length followed by indices.
The final two rows record factory-call identity, cloned-handle identity,
mutation seen by original, untouched independent allocation, and retained alias.

Capture implementation: tools/oracle/martensite_meshvs_volume_topology.cxx.
Build commands, compiler declaration IDs, hashes, platform and scope exclusions:
porting/runtime-evidence/meshvs-volume-topology-2026-10-14/scope.json.
This fixture stays with the Rust tests if removable oracle infrastructure goes away.
Tests read it with include_str! and have no OCCT source/build/runtime dependency.
No original upstream test directly invoking these two methods was found; these
are newly generated native regression cases, not claimed legacy translations.

Immutable unpublished candidate revision (2026-10-14):
The first 24 rows remain exact connectivity/order and rejected-input evidence.
The final two rows remain unchanged historical evidence of OCCT mutable handle
semantics. Martensite does not replay those ownership semantics: successful
factories now return private owned Rust vectors with immutable face slices,
value equality, independent deep clones and no shared mutable state. Counts below
three return typed TooFewBasePoints errors rather than a null handle. Bounds and
allocation failures are explicit typed errors; native failure parity is not claimed.
No live native program was consulted or executed for this revision. Independent
closed-connectivity, edge-orientation, Euler and node-set checks supplement the
historical fixture. This is visualization connectivity, not accepted solid geometry.
